pr_title: Update Apple TV integration to support tvOS 15
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This bumps pyatv to the latest version (0.9.7) and makes various adjustments to follow the more generalized API. This mainly concerns the pairing process as that is completely general now, with no special cases where protocol X or Y must be paired or it won't work. Another improvement is that each protocol is verified if pairing or password is needed and provides proper action or error message accordingly.

Change log for pyatv is here: https://github.com/postlund/pyatv/releases/tag/v0.9.0 (0.9.0 has the most important changes, following versions are just minor fixes)

https://github.com/postlund/pyatv/compare/v0.8.2...v0.9.7

The gist of what this update brings:

* Support for tvOS 15 in general
* All device types that pyatv currently supports (Apple TV all generations, HomePods, AirPort Express, iTunes/Music app on macOS and most AirPlay v1 receivers)
* Local streaming of files to the receiver via AirPlay (RAOP)
* AirPlay support for generic receivers is limited, e.g. streaming files is supported, stop button and metadata is updated when Home Assistant is streaming but not when someone else is streaming (limitation in AirPlay)
* I have added a "force re-auth" flag to config flow options to re-trigger set up, which might be needed if a protocol failed to pair the first time (e.g. access control prevented it).

There are a few question marks on my end that I need help with:

* There is no migration path for existing config entries. Old entries must be removed and devices added again. This is simply because the (unique) identifier used to discover the device was part of the MRP protocol, which Apple has removed. So Home Assistant will just keep looking for a device that doesn't exist. I have made this more future proof by saving all identifiers in the config entry, so this will not happen again in the future. How should I handle this now though?
* I would somehow like to raise `ConfigEntryAuthFailed` when authentication fails, but that is only possible in `async_setup_entry`. Since I have a connect loop in a background task, that is not possible. I'm not sure what to do.
* One feature lots of people have requested is TTS support for the HomePod. By supporting audio streaming, that is technically possible but the problem is that only local streaming is supported, i.e. the source must be a local file. The way TTS works today caches the output speech as a file but pass on a URL to `play_media`, so it doesn't work in my case. I did a hack (which obviously should not be in the code) that, when a URL to a TTS-file is passed to `play_media`, extracts the filename and waits for that particular file to appear on disk. This works, but it's not very pretty, so I would prefer a better solution to this. I have a discussion in architecture [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/576).

I think that's it for now.

It's a catch-22 because current changes to the manifest will not work as AirPlay devices are not found. Since tvOS 15 MRP (used for remote control support) is tunneled over AirPlay, which means that it must be added to the manifest. This however means other AirPlay devices are discovered as well. So the filter provided by @bdraco is needed to just filter out Apple TV devices. Otherwise we need a hack in the config flow that does more or less the same thing.

From Home Assistant is what I'm referring to. The reason is described in the initial post:

*There is no migration path for existing config entries. Old entries must be removed and devices added again. This is simply because the (unique) identifier used to discover the device was part of the MRP protocol, which Apple has removed. So Home Assistant will just keep looking for a device that doesn't exist. I have made this more future proof by saving all identifiers in the config entry, so this will not happen again in the future. How should I handle this now though?*

If it is possible to remove it, then we probably should. But I don't know how to do that properly and AFAIK there's no developer documentation describing how to do this or even if it's a practice to do so.

I think we should re-configure all config entries that don't have the stored identifiers. I commented about that here:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/58665#discussion_r739010570

The problem is that we can't reconfigure as we don't have any information to match a config entry to its corresponding device on the network. The information is disjunctive. I'm up for suggestions to solve it.

We can ask the user for any information we need in the config flow. How would we do it for a new device? If we can configure new devices we should be able to solve this. If we can't find a matching device in the end of the flow, we can remove the config entry and let the user know.
Ok, I will see if I can change things around a bit and make that happen. I think it deviates a bit from how it works right now, so it probably needs some work.

Took some time to come around with this because of life. But I have made some updates to pyatv and fixed so the MRP identifier discovered again, so no breaking change needs to happen. An integration must be removed and re-added to pair new protocols though since it's not possible to manually trigger re-configuration. I still believe this is something that Home assistant core should offer (not for further discussion here).

I have also implemented initial support for audio streaming from HTTP(S) in pyatv and made a minor tweak, which means TTS works without any hacks now.
